name: Slite
subcategory: notes, wikis and personal knowledge bases
tagline: Create a clean team wiki with documents, collections, search, and lightweight answers

pricing.notes: Typical Standard seat price; annual billing can be lower.

tiers.name: Basic
tiers.limits: Unlimited documents; 200 MB per file; 5 GB storage/user; 30 Ask questions/seat/month; 30 AI edits/user/month.
tiers.notes: Public page exposes $10/user/month billed annually; a month-to-month price was not exposed.

tiers.name: Pro
tiers.limits: Unlimited file-upload size; 10 GB storage/user; 50 monthly AI credits/seat; unlimited AI edits.
tiers.notes: Public page exposes $20/user/month billed annually; a month-to-month price was not exposed.

tiers.name: Enterprise
tiers.limits: 10 GB storage/user; reader-only seats and enterprise security; numeric seat minimum and price are quote-based.

pricing.freeTierCaps: no free tier; 14-day trial with no card, then a paid plan is required
pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual; live public page exposes annual rates only
pricing.hiddenCosts: seats added during a term are charged on the next invoice or prorated; removing seats reduces only the next renewal rather than the current annual commitment

verdictSummary: The core loop is buildable, but a dependable replacement becomes a real weekend or multi-day project. For Slite, create a clean team wiki with documents, collections, search, and lightweight answers. The hard boundary is team search, permissions, integrations, ai answers, and polished collaborative editing, plus sync, collaboration, and capture polish.
coreLoopDIY: Create a team wiki of linked documents organized into collections, search them instantly, surface backlinks, and export a normal Markdown folder.
requirements: optional sync folder chosen by the user
whatYouLose: team search, permissions, integrations, AI answers, and polished collaborative editing
ongoingBurden: file watching, conflict handling, indexing, mobile apps, encryption, backups, and migrations
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Slite because people keep paying when the note system is trusted across every device and disappears into their daily capture habits. The recurring cost buys file watching, conflict handling, indexing, mobile apps, encryption, backups, and migrations, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: AppFlowy
priorArt.desc: Active open-source workspace with local-first documents and databases.

alternatives.name: BookStack
alternatives.desc: Simple team documentation with rigid shelves and no per-seat toll.

facts.install: Fresh Ubuntu install script or manual PHP/MySQL setup
facts.dataFormat: Pages, users, permissions, and settings in MySQL/MariaDB; uploaded images and files in the server filesystem or configured object storage
facts.gapVsPaid: It lacks Slite's hosted zero-admin experience and polished AI-assisted answers, document verification and knowledge-maintenance workflow, while imposing a rigid hierarchy.
facts.setupBlocker: The official script expects a fresh Ubuntu host; manual installs require PHP extensions, a database, writable storage, mail, and TLS

alternatives.name: Docmost
alternatives.desc: A clean collaborative wiki with spaces, comments, history and search.

facts.install: Hosted signup or Docker Compose with PostgreSQL and Redis
facts.dataFormat: Pages, users, comments, and history in PostgreSQL; jobs/cache in Redis; attachments in a persistent local volume by default or S3/Azure Blob
facts.gapVsPaid: It covers collaborative pages well but does not match Slite's mature AI answers, document verification and managed team knowledge workflow without self-hosting work.
facts.setupBlocker: Self-hosting requires Docker, a strong APP_SECRET, database credentials, persistent volumes, and normally a domain, TLS reverse proxy, and SMTP

alternatives.name: Wiki.js
alternatives.desc: A full team wiki with good search and enough knobs to justify Docker.

facts.install: Docker Compose with PostgreSQL, or a Node.js package plus a supported database
facts.dataFormat: Pages, users, authentication data, and history in the configured database; optional storage modules can mirror content and assets to Git, local disk, or cloud storage
facts.gapVsPaid: It is a flexible wiki, but Slite is easier to adopt and offers more polished hosted search, AI answers and knowledge-maintenance features with no server administration.
facts.setupBlocker: You must provision a database and persistent volumes, then configure backups and a TLS reverse proxy for public use

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Standard plan and a personal local knowledge base DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a personal replacement for Slite in an empty repository.
Use Tauri 2, React, TypeScript, SQLite, and Markdown files as the source of truth; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: create a team wiki of linked documents organized into collections, search them instantly, surface backlinks, and export a normal Markdown folder.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Store one Markdown file per note and a small SQLite index that can be rebuilt at any time.
Support wiki links, tags, backlinks, daily notes, pinned notes, and full-text search.
Add a fast command palette and keyboard-first create, rename, move, and link actions.
Render Markdown with task lists, code blocks, tables, and local image attachments.
Detect external file changes and show a safe conflict-resolution view.
Provide full-folder export, import, and an index-rebuild command.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Deliberately leave out proprietary sync servers.
Deliberately leave out real-time multiplayer documents.
Deliberately leave out a plugin marketplace and hosted public sites.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
